# 'bolero install pkg@version' works outside a module.
env BOLERO_MODULE=auto
bolero install example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0
exists $BOLERO_PATH/bin/a$GOEXE
rm $BOLERO_PATH/bin


# 'bolero install pkg@version' reports an error if modules are disabled.
env BOLERO_MODULE=off
! bolero install example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0
stderr '^bolero: modules disabled by BOLERO_MODULE=off; see ''bolero help modules''$'
env BOLERO_MODULE=auto


# 'bolero install pkg@version' ignores go.mod in current directory.
cd m
cp go.mod go.mod.orig
! bolero list -m all
stderr '^bolero: example.com/cmd@v1.1.0-doesnotexist: reading http.*/mod/example.com/cmd/@v/v1.1.0-doesnotexist.info: 404 Not Found\n\tserver response: 404 page not found$'
stderr '^bolero: example.com/cmd@v1.1.0-doesnotexist: missing go.sum entry for go.mod file; to add it:\n\tbolero mod download example.com/cmd$'
bolero install example.com/cmd/a@latest
cmp go.mod go.mod.orig
exists $BOLERO_PATH/bin/a$GOEXE
bolero version -m $BOLERO_PATH/bin/a$GOEXE
stdout '^\tmod\texample.com/cmd\tv1.0.0\t' # "latest", not from go.mod
rm $BOLERO_PATH/bin/a
cd ..


# 'bolero install -modfile=x.mod pkg@version' reports an error, but only if
# -modfile is specified explicitly on the command line.
cd m
env BOLERO_FLAGS=-modfile=go.mod
bolero install example.com/cmd/a@latest  # same as above
env BOLERO_FLAGS=
! bolero install -modfile=go.mod example.com/cmd/a@latest
stderr '^bolero: -modfile cannot be used with commands that ignore the current module$'
cd ..


# Every test case requires linking, so we only cover the most important cases
# when -short is set.
[short] stop


# 'bolero install pkg@version' works on a module that doesn't have a go.mod file
# and with a module whose go.mod file has missing requirements.
# With a proxy, the two cases are indistinguishable.
bolero install rsc.io/fortune@v1.0.0
stderr '^bolero: found rsc.io/quote in rsc.io/quote v1.5.2$'
exists $BOLERO_PATH/bin/fortune$GOEXE
! exists $BOLERO_PATH/pkg/mod/rsc.io/fortune@v1.0.0/go.mod # no go.mod file
bolero version -m $BOLERO_PATH/bin/fortune$GOEXE
stdout '^\tdep\trsc.io/quote\tv1.5.2\t' # latest version of fortune's dependency
rm $BOLERO_PATH/bin


# 'bolero install dir@version' works like a normal 'bolero install' command if
# dir is a relative or absolute path.
env BOLERO_MODULE=on
bolero mod download rsc.io/fortune@v1.0.0
! bolero install $BOLERO_PATH/pkg/mod/rsc.io/fortune@v1.0.0
stderr '^bolero: go\.mod file not found in current directory or any parent directory; see ''bolero help modules''$'
! bolero install ../pkg/mod/rsc.io/fortune@v1.0.0
stderr '^bolero: go\.mod file not found in current directory or any parent directory; see ''bolero help modules''$'
mkdir tmp
cd tmp
bolero mod init -modfile=go.mod tmp
bolero mod edit -require=rsc.io/fortune@v1.0.0
! bolero install -mod=readonly $BOLERO_PATH/pkg/mod/rsc.io/fortune@v1.0.0
stderr '^missing go\.sum entry for module providing package rsc\.io/fortune; to add:\n\tbolero mod download rsc\.io/fortune$'
! bolero install -mod=readonly ../../pkg/mod/rsc.io/fortune@v1.0.0
stderr '^missing go\.sum entry for module providing package rsc\.io/fortune; to add:\n\tbolero mod download rsc\.io/fortune$'
bolero get rsc.io/fortune@v1.0.0
bolero install -mod=readonly $BOLERO_PATH/pkg/mod/rsc.io/fortune@v1.0.0
exists $BOLERO_PATH/bin/fortune$GOEXE
cd ..
rm tmp
rm $BOLERO_PATH/bin
env BOLERO_MODULE=auto

# 'bolero install pkg@version' reports errors for meta packages, std packages,
# and directories.
! bolero install std@v1.0.0
stderr '^bolero: std@v1.0.0: argument must be a package path, not a meta-package$'
! bolero install fmt@v1.0.0
stderr '^bolero: fmt@v1.0.0: argument must not be a package in the standard library$'
! bolero install example.com//cmd/a@v1.0.0
stderr '^bolero: example.com//cmd/a@v1.0.0: argument must be a clean package path$'
! bolero install example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0 ./x@v1.0.0
stderr '^bolero: ./x@v1.0.0: argument must be a package path, not a relative path$'
! bolero install example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0 $BOLERO_PATH/src/x@v1.0.0
stderr '^bolero: '$WORK'[/\\]gopath/src/x@v1.0.0: argument must be a package path, not an absolute path$'
! bolero install example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0 cmd/...@v1.0.0
stderr '^package cmd/go not provided by module example.com/cmd@v1.0.0$'

# 'bolero install pkg@version' should accept multiple arguments but report an error
# if the version suffixes are different, even if they refer to the same version.
bolero install example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0 example.com/cmd/b@v1.0.0
exists $BOLERO_PATH/bin/a$GOEXE
exists $BOLERO_PATH/bin/b$GOEXE
rm $BOLERO_PATH/bin

env BOLERO_MODULE=on
bolero list -m example.com/cmd@latest
stdout '^example.com/cmd v1.0.0$'
env BOLERO_MODULE=auto

! bolero install example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0 example.com/cmd/b@latest
stderr '^bolero: example.com/cmd/b@latest: all arguments must refer to packages in the same module at the same version \(@v1.0.0\)$'


# 'bolero install pkg@version' should report an error if the arguments are in
# different modules.
! bolero install example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0 rsc.io/fortune@v1.0.0
stderr '^package rsc.io/fortune provided by module rsc.io/fortune@v1.0.0\n\tAll packages must be provided by the same module \(example.com/cmd@v1.0.0\).$'


# 'bolero install pkg@version' should report an error if an argument is not
# a main package.
! bolero install example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0 example.com/cmd/err@v1.0.0
stderr '^package example.com/cmd/err is not a main package$'

# Wildcards should match only main packages. This module has a non-main package
# with an error, so we'll know if that gets built.
mkdir tmp
cd tmp
bolero mod init -modfile=go.mod m
bolero get example.com/cmd@v1.0.0
! bolero build example.com/cmd/...
stderr 'err[/\\]err.go:3:9: undefined: DoesNotCompile( .*)?$'
cd ..

bolero install example.com/cmd/...@v1.0.0
exists $BOLERO_PATH/bin/a$GOEXE
exists $BOLERO_PATH/bin/b$GOEXE
rm $BOLERO_PATH/bin

# If a wildcard matches no packages, we should see a warning.
! bolero install example.com/cmd/nomatch...@v1.0.0
stderr '^bolero: example.com/cmd/nomatch\.\.\.@v1.0.0: module example.com/cmd@v1.0.0 found, but does not contain packages matching example.com/cmd/nomatch\.\.\.$'
bolero install example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0 example.com/cmd/nomatch...@v1.0.0
stderr '^bolero: warning: "example.com/cmd/nomatch\.\.\." matched no packages$'

# If a wildcard matches only non-main packages, we should see a different warning.
bolero install example.com/cmd/err...@v1.0.0
stderr '^bolero: warning: "example.com/cmd/err\.\.\." matched only non-main packages$'


# 'bolero install pkg@version' should report errors if the module contains
# replace or exclude directives.
bolero mod download example.com/cmd@v1.0.0-replace
! bolero install example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0-replace
cmp stderr replace-err

bolero mod download example.com/cmd@v1.0.0-exclude
! bolero install example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0-exclude
cmp stderr exclude-err

# 'bolero install pkg@version' should report an error if the module requires a
# higher version of itself.
! bolero install example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0-newerself
stderr '^bolero: example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0-newerself: version constraints conflict:\n\texample.com/cmd@v1.0.0-newerself requires example.com/cmd@v1.0.0, but v1.0.0-newerself is requested$'


# 'bolero install pkg@version' will only match a retracted version if it's
# explicitly requested.
env BOLERO_MODULE=on
bolero list -m -versions example.com/cmd
! stdout v1.9.0
bolero list -m -versions -retracted example.com/cmd
stdout v1.9.0
bolero install example.com/cmd/a@latest
bolero version -m $BOLERO_PATH/bin/a$GOEXE
stdout '^\tmod\texample.com/cmd\tv1.0.0\t'
bolero install example.com/cmd/a@v1.9.0
bolero version -m $BOLERO_PATH/bin/a$GOEXE
stdout '^\tmod\texample.com/cmd\tv1.9.0\t'
env BOLERO_MODULE=

# 'bolero install pkg@version' succeeds when -mod=readonly is set explicitly.
# Verifies #43278.
bolero install -mod=readonly example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0


# 'bolero install pkg@version' should show a deprecation message if the module is deprecated.
env BOLERO_MODULE=on
bolero install example.com/deprecated/a/cmd/a@latest
stderr '^bolero: module example.com/deprecated/a is deprecated: in example.com/deprecated/a@v1.9.0$'
bolero install example.com/deprecated/a/cmd/a@v1.0.0
stderr '^bolero: module example.com/deprecated/a is deprecated: in example.com/deprecated/a@v1.9.0$'

# 'bolero install pkg@version' does not show a deprecation message if the module is no longer
# deprecated in its latest version, even if the module is deprecated in its current version.
bolero install example.com/undeprecated/cmd/a@v1.0.0
! stderr 'module.*is deprecated'

-- m/go.mod --
module m

go 1.16

require example.com/cmd v1.1.0-doesnotexist
-- x/x.go --
package main

func main() {}
-- replace-err --
bolero: example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0-replace (in example.com/cmd@v1.0.0-replace):
	The go.mod file for the module providing named packages contains one or
	more replace directives. It must not contain directives that would cause
	it to be interpreted differently than if it were the main module.
-- exclude-err --
bolero: example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0-exclude (in example.com/cmd@v1.0.0-exclude):
	The go.mod file for the module providing named packages contains one or
	more exclude directives. It must not contain directives that would cause
	it to be interpreted differently than if it were the main module.
